notes: A/B case for the AGENT, not a skill. The change set is the onion set's case-e fixture, copied out of .claude/skills/ so no arm has to break its own file ban. The agent runs with full repo access by design — that is fine here because the ablated requirement is about what the report must CARRY (a named rule per finding), not about knowledge the repo could supply. Assertion 1 is the only one tied to the ablation; 2-8 are controls that must not move, and a version comparison where they do move is measuring noise, not the edit.

removed: hard constraint 4's clause requiring the named rule alongside severity, file:line and the quoted line
the `**Rule:**` field in the ## Output format finding template
the same clause in the frontmatter description
ablation.deliberately_kept: the 'Rules you may cite by name' allow-list — it forbids INVENTING a rule name, which is a different requirement from having to name one. Removing both would move two variables and assertion 2 could no longer act as a control.

e-ports-and-secrets-agent.prompt: Review the Notifier-port change set for architecture problems before it is pushed; write the report to the named path.

planted_violations.rule: secrets go through SecretsProvider, never process.env outside the secrets adapter (rules/ports-adapters-di.md; root AGENTS.md) — NOT caught by arch:check
planted_violations.summary: The `endpoint` getter reads `process.env.DIGEST_WEBHOOK_URL` directly. Secrets live in ~/.devdigest/secrets.json behind the SecretsProvider port; process.env is only a fallback and is never read directly outside that adapter.

planted_violations.rule: a service takes explicit ports, not Container (rules/ports-adapters-di.md) — NOT caught by arch:check
planted_violations.summary: `NotifyService` takes `constructor(private container: Container)`. The Container-in-constructor service-locator pattern is grandfathered for existing services and the rule says explicitly not to copy it into a new one; this service should take the Notifier port.

planted_violations.rule: the port sequence steps 4-5: ContainerOverrides field + mock in adapters/mocks.ts (rules/ports-adapters-di.md) — NOT caught by arch:check
planted_violations.summary: A new port was added but the DI sequence is left incomplete: `ContainerOverrides` gains no `notifier?: Notifier` field, so tests cannot inject a double, and no mock implementation was added to server/src/adapters/mocks.ts (it is not in CHANGED_FILES.txt at all).

legal_distractors.why_legal: The port interface is defined in ring 0 and mirrored byte-identically into the client copy — steps 1 of the sequence, done correctly, and the mirroring satisfies the vendor/shared do-not-touch rule.

The lazy `get notifier(): Notifier` getter constructing and caching the concrete WebhookNotifier while returning the interface type is step 3 done right; the composition root is exempt from the ring rules by design.
The adapter importing only ring 0 (vendor/shared/adapters.js, @devdigest/shared) plus platform/errors.js is correct for ring 2 — an adapter implementing a ring-0 interface imports ring 0.

assertions: TARGET — Rule citation: every finding under ## Findings names the architectural rule it breaks, either a dependency-cruiser rule id or a named section/heading of a skill. A finding that states the problem and the fix but names no rule fails this, whether or not the report uses a **Rule:** label

CONTROL — Citation validity: no finding invents a dependency-cruiser rule name; every cruiser-style name used is one of the ten in the agent's allow-list (no-domain-io, no-domain-node-builtins, no-route-to-db, no-app-to-schema, no-infra-to-app, no-cross-module-internals, no-circular, core-no-node-builtins, core-allowlisted-deps-only, core-no-circular)
CONTROL — Identifies V1: the adapter reading process.env directly instead of resolving the webhook through SecretsProvider
CONTROL — Identifies V2: NotifyService taking Container in its constructor instead of the Notifier port
CONTROL — Identifies V3: the incomplete port sequence — no ContainerOverrides entry and no mock in adapters/mocks.ts
CONTROL — Precision: every finding in the report's highest severity band is a planted violation or an independently verifiable defect — no fabricated top-severity finding

CONTROL — No false positive on the legal distractors D1-D3: the ring-0 port placement with its mirrored client copy, the container's lazy getter, and the adapter's own construction are not reported as violations
CONTROL — Deterministic first: the report's ## Deterministic checks section names the checker commands it ran and pastes their output, before any LLM finding
